title: Vitamin patches – level 3
paragraphs: The dietary supplement market is a 60 billion dollar industry, and a new trend is just coming: wearable vitamin patches.

The brand Barriére is leading this movement and expects to double its revenue to 10 million dollars in 2026. This growth is driven by a massive deal to sell their products in 1,700 Walmart stores and the launch of the world’s first patch for lactose intolerance. The company targets younger consumers through social media and offers a stylish alternative to swallowing pills. The patches work transdermally – skin heat activates the ingredients so they enter the bloodstream directly.

However, health experts point out that there is no clinical evidence for vitamin patches compared to traditional oral supplements. Because the US government classifies supplements as food rather than drugs, companies are not legally required to make large medical trials. To build consumer trust, Barriére manufactures its products in regulated facilities in the UK and uses independent third-party labs for voluntary safety testing.
